'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Islamic terrorism in Europe]]
**[[2023 Brussels shooting]]
***Two [[Sweden|Swedish]] nationals are killed and another is injured during a shooting in [[Brussels]], [[Belgium]]. The perpetrator, [[Tunisians|Tunisian]] Abdesalem Lassoued, an [[Islamic State]] sympathizer, flees the scene. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/two-swedes-shot-dead-brussels-police-2023-10-16/ (Reuters)]
*[[Islamist insurgency in the Sahel]]
**[[Mali War]]
***The [[United Nations peacekeeping]] mission in [[Mali]], [[United Nations Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in Mali|MINUSMA]], initiates a withdrawal from two camps in [[Aguelhok]] and [[Tessalit]], [[Kidal Region]]. [https://english.ahram.org.eg/NewsContent/2/10/510351/World/Africa/UN-peacekeepers-leave-two-camps-in-tense-northern-.aspx (AFP via ''Al-Ahram'')]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**[[Gaza war|Israel–Hamas war]]
***[[Evacuations during the Gaza war]]
****The [[World Health Organization]] says that 21 hospitals in [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]] have been ordered to [[emergency evacuation|evacuate]] by [[Israel]], warning that this "may amount to a violation of international humanitarian law". [https://www.ft.com/content/8376c8bc-4ce4-433b-912c-337bf2ca66e6 (Financial Times)]
****[[Israel]] begins evacuating 28 communities located within two kilometers of [[Blue Line (withdrawal line)|the border]] with [[Lebanon]] amid clashes with [[Hezbollah]]. [https://www.foxnews.com/world/israel-evacuating-28-communities-lebanon-border (Fox News)]
****Hundreds of [[Americans]] are evacuated by sea from [[Haifa]], Israel, to [[Cyprus]]. [https://www.thejc.com/news/israel/us-citizens-evacuated-by-sea-via-haifa-port-7q9UnNmw96PHh0HX7IzdfZ (''The Jewish Chronicle'')]
***[[List of journalists killed in the Gaza war|Journalists killed in the Israel–Hamas war]]
****Muhammad al-Najjar, a member of the [[Board of Directors]] of the national authority for the documentation and [[prosecution]] of crimes committed by the [[Israeli government]], is killed in an Israeli [[airstrike]], along with 16 members of his family. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2023/10/15/israel-hamas-war-live-gaza-hospitals-fuel-to-last-24-more-hours-un-says (Al Jazeera)]
****Eleven Palestinian journalists have been killed by the [[Israeli military]] and more than 20 others have been injured, according to the Palestinian Journalists Syndicate. [https://tribune.com.pk/story/2441396/11-journalists-killed-over-20-injured-in-gaza-since-oct-7-palestinian-journalists-group (The Express Tribune)]
***[[Gaza war hostage crisis|Israel–Hamas war hostage crisis]]
****Hamas releases the first video of a [[hostage]] on [[Telegram (software)|Telegram]] since the war started, a 21-year-old Israeli woman from [[Shoham]] who was kidnapped during the [[Nova music festival massacre|Re'im music festival massacre]]. In the video, the woman claims to be receiving medical treatment from her captors. [https://www.jpost.com/breaking-news/article-768707 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
***[[Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip (2023–present)|2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip]]
****The World Health Organization announces that there are only 24 hours of water, electricity, and fuel remaining in Gaza. [https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/israel-hamas-war-gaza-strip/ (CBS News)]
****[[Medical Aid for Palestinians]] says that hospitals in Gaza are currently facing a "catastrophic" shortage of medical supplies with the [[United Nations]] also reporting that at least four hospitals in northern Gaza are no longer operational because of Israeli bombings. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2023/10/15/israel-hamas-war-live-gaza-hospitals-fuel-to-last-24-more-hours-un-says (Al Jazeera)]
****The chief of the UN agency for Palestine, [[UNRWA]], announces it can no longer deliver assistance to the hundreds of thousands of people in need in Gaza. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2023/10/16/unrwa-palestine-gaza-un-refugee/ (The Washington Post)]
****[[Sameh Shoukry]], [[Egypt]]'s [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Egypt)|Minister of Foreign Affairs]], announces that [[US]]-backed efforts to re-open the [[Rafah border crossing]] have failed, citing Israel's refusal to guarantee the safety of incoming aid convoys and outgoing foreign nationals. [https://www.reuters.com/world/egypt-us-israel-agree-ceasefire-southern-gaza-opening-rafah-crossing-0600-gmt-2023-10-16/ (Reuters)] [https://www.cnn.com/middleeast/live-news/israel-news-hamas-war-10-16-23/h_ddef200ffa8657a9a77392febeb97a9c (CNN)]
****The United Nations reports that more than 400,000 Palestinians are sheltering in UN schools and buildings in the Gaza Strip and that fourteen [[UNRWA]] personnel have been killed in Israeli airstrikes. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2023/10/15/israel-hamas-war-live-gaza-hospitals-fuel-to-last-24-more-hours-un-says (Al Jazeera)]
****Palestinians [[Gaza war protests|protest]] in several cities across the [[West Bank]] calling for an end to Israeli attacks on Gaza. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2023/10/15/israel-hamas-war-live-gaza-hospitals-fuel-to-last-24-more-hours-un-says (Al Jazeera)]
****The [[UNRWA]] retracts its statements concerning looting by Hamas affiliates, clarifying that they have confirmed no theft had taken place, after a prior announcement that men claiming to be from Hamas stole fuel and medicine from their offices in Gaza. Subsequently, Israeli journalist [[Barak Ravid]] claims to have received additional confirmation from sources within the [[United Nations]] that such theft did, in fact, occur. [https://www.thejc.com/news/israel/un-says-men-claiming-to-be-hamas-authorities-took-fuel-and-medicine-from-gaza-city-compound-5RNz7AWxYYgXR7Ll1MniyI (Jewish Chronicle)] [https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/israel-hamas-war-gaza-palestinians-hostages-updates/#post-update-34ebdad7 (CBS News)] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/un-refugee-agency-says-hamas-stole-fuel-and-medications-from-its-gaza-premises/ (Times of Israel)]
***At least six civilians are killed and eight others are injured in airstrikes near [[Khan Younis]] and at least seven people, including five [[emergency workers]], are killed in Israeli airstrikes on two civil defense facilities in [[Gaza City]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2023/10/15/israel-hamas-war-live-gaza-hospitals-fuel-to-last-24-more-hours-un-says (Al Jazeera)]
***At least four people, including three children, are killed as a result of an Israeli airstrike on the [[UN]] Nuseirat [[refugee camp]] in central Gaza. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2023/10/15/israel-hamas-war-live-gaza-hospitals-fuel-to-last-24-more-hours-un-says (Al Jazeera)]
***Hamas [[Izz ad-Din al-Qassam Brigades|forces]] launch [[missile]]s at the two largest [[Israeli cities]], [[Tel Aviv]] and [[Jerusalem]], saying that this was in response to Israel's "targeting of [[civilian]]s". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/world-middle-east-67119233 (BBC News)]
***Israeli military forces carry out raids in multiple areas in the West Bank, including [[East Jerusalem]], [[Nablus]], [[Bethlehem]], and [[Hebron]], arresting around 600 people. Most are held without charges under "administrative detention", where the individuals are not told the reasons for their arrest.  [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2023/10/15/israel-hamas-war-live-gaza-hospitals-fuel-to-last-24-more-hours-un-says (Al Jazeera)]
***Hamas [[Majlis-ash-Shura|Shura Council]] member [[Osama Mazini]], who was in charge of negotiation affairs concerning the [[prisoner of war|captured]] Israeli soldier [[Gilad Shalit]], is killed in an airstrike in the Gaza Strip. [https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/378626 (Israel National News)]
**A report by a UN-mandated investigative body has found that Israeli forces used "lethal force without justification" when they shot and killed [[Al Jazeera Media Network|Al Jazeera]] journalist [[Shireen Abu Akleh]] in the [[West Bank]] last year. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/10/16/israeli-forces-killed-abu-akleh-without-justification-un-inquiry-says (Al Jazeera)]
**[[2024 Iran–Israel conflict]], [[Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)|Israel–Hezbollah conflict]]
***Nine [[Lebanon|Lebanese]] civilians injured by IDF fired [[white phosphorus munitions]] on [[Dhayra]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/amnesty-international-israeli-forces-wounded-lebanese-civilians-white-104521713 (ABCNews)]

'''International relations'''
*[[China–Philippines relations]]
**[[Territorial disputes in the South China Sea]]
***The [[Armed Forces of the Philippines|Philippine military]] demands that [[China]] stop "dangerous and offensive" actions in the [[South China Sea]] after a [[People's Liberation Army Navy]] ship performed "aggressive maneuvers" near the disputed [[Thitu Island]] last week. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/philippines-denounces-china-dangerous-offensive-actions-south-china-sea-2023-10-16/ (Reuters)]
*[[International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[Colombia–Israel relations]]
***[[Colombia]] requests the departure of the [[List of Israeli ambassadors|Israeli ambassador]] following [[President of Colombia|Colombian President]] [[Gustavo Petro]]'s remarks criticizing Israel's actions. In response, [[Israel]] suspends [[Arms industry|security exports]] to Colombia. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/middle-east/20231016-colombia-demands-israel-envoy-leave-amid-spat-over-war-with-hamas (AFP via RFI)]
**[[Israel–Pakistan relations]]
***[[Minister for Foreign Affairs (Pakistan)|Pakistani Foreign Minister]] [[Jalil Abbas Jilani]] condemns the Israeli bombing on [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]], equating the actions with [[genocide]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/10/15/which-countries-have-criticised-israeli-attacks-on-gaza. (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Israel–United States relations]]
***[[US Secretary of State]] [[Antony Blinken]] visits Israel and reaffirms American support for Israel. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-67124831 (BBC News)]
**[[Arab League]] Secretary-General [[Ahmed Aboul Gheit]] calls for an immediate end to military operations in Gaza and for aid to be allowed into the enclave. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/arab-league-chief-demands-end-to-idfs-military-operations-in-gaza. (Times of Israel)] 
**The [[China International Development Cooperation Agency]] announces that they will provide emergency humanitarian aid to the [[UNRWA|UN Palestine agency]] and the [[Palestinian Authority]]. [https://www.thestandard.com.hk/breaking-news-print/209320/China-is-providing-emergency-humanitarian-aid-for-Palestinian-refugees---state-media (Reuters via ''The Standard'')]
**Around 25,000 people demonstrate in [[Cotabato]], [[Philippines]], to express solidarity with [[Palestinians]] and to condemn Israel's air raids on the Gaza Strip. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/thousands-join-pro-palestine-protest-in-southern-philippines (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]
*[[Japan–Russia relations]]
**[[Russia]] suspends imports of [[Agriculture, forestry, and fishing in Japan#Fisheries|Japanese seafood]] due to concerns over [[Discharge of radioactive water of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant|wastewater discharges]] from the [[Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Plant]]. [https://www.jordantimes.com/news/business/after-china-russia-suspends-japanese-seafood-imports (AFP via ''The Jordan Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Anti-corruption campaign under Xi Jinping]]
**Former [[Bank of China]] chair [[Liu Lian'ge]] is arrested on allegations of [[Corruption in China|corruption]]. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2023/10/17/business/foreign-business/ex-bank-of-china-chair-arrested-for-corruption/1915072 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]
*[[Israel–Hamas war protests]]
**Around 49 [[Anti-war movement|anti-war]] protesters calling for [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] to press for a ceasefire are arrested outside the [[White House]] by [[United States Secret Service|U.S. Secret Service]] members. [https://www.axios.com/2023/10/17/jewish-protest-white-house-israel-hamas-war-arrests (Axios)]  
*[[Australia]]'s [[internet safety]] commissioner fines American [[technology company]] [[X Corp.]] for [[Australian dollar|AU$]]610,500 ([[United States dollar|US$]]385,000) for inadequately addressing [[child sexual abuse]] content on [[Twitter]]. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2023/10/17/business/foreign-business/australia-fines-musks-x/1915074 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 Indonesian presidential election]]
**The [[Constitutional Court of Indonesia]] rules that regional leaders under the age of 40 can run for [[President of Indonesia|president]] or [[Vice President of Indonesia|vice president]], thus allowing President [[Joko Widodo]]'s son [[Gibran Rakabuming Raka]] to run as a Vice Presidential candidate in the next presidential election. [https://www.thejakartapost.com/indonesia/2023/10/16/breaking-constitutional-court-opens-door-for-jokowis-son-to-run-in-presidential-poll.html (''The Jakarta Post'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 Winter Olympics]]
**The [[Italian Olympic Committee]] announces that [[bobsleigh]], [[luge]], and [[Skeleton (sport)|skeleton]] events will not be held in [[Italy]] due to the high costs of rebuilding the [[Eugenio Monti olympic track|Eugenio Monti Olympic Track]] in [[Cortina d'Ampezzo]]. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/winter-sports/67120057 (BBC News)]
*[[2028 Summer Olympics]]
**The [[International Olympic Committee]] approves the inclusion of [[cricket]], [[flag football]], [[lacrosse]], [[Squash (sport)|squash]], and [[baseball]]/[[softball]] at the 2028 [[Summer Olympics]] in [[Los Angeles]]. [https://www.skysports.com/cricket/news/15234/12985395/international-olympic-committee-approves-cricket-and-four-other-sports-for-2028-games-in-los-angeles (Sky Sports)]
